subject: Cost of Living Approval for Trump Falls to 17% in New AP Poll
posts:
A new AP-NORC poll reveals a staggering collapse in public trust, with Donald Trump's cost-of-living approval plummeting to just 17% as economic realities bite ahead of the midterms. 🌐
Evidence: Economic Relief, Rising Prices, Political Survival
#Aletheia #USPol

The administration claims its policies are designed to lower inflation, secure energy independence, and establish global tech leadership through initiatives like the new Super Intelligence Force.
Stated Judgement: (+0.85, +0.15) — Good Preference

In reality, 82% of Americans disapprove of Trump's economic handling. Geopolitical strikes on Iran have driven up gas prices, while flashy tech task forces serve as a distraction from systemic domestic strain.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.82, -0.78) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction. The administration's economic promises have collapsed under the weight of inflationary military actions and superficial policy distractions.
Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 8.20, z: 3)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Economic Policy: FAIL (-0.85, -0.80) — High gas prices.
- Super Intelligence Force: COND (-0.20, -0.10) — PR stunt.
- Geopolitical Strategy: FAIL (-0.90, -0.85) — Iran strike costs.

With the 2026 midterms approaching, a new AP-NORC poll shows Trump's overall approval at a career-low 31%. Voters are directly blaming administration policies, including a February strike on Iran, for persistent high prices.

The Poison:
While the administration attempts to frame the February strike on Iran as a necessary sacrifice for national security, the immediate consequence is a severe domestic energy tax that disproportionately harms working-class families.

The Breakdown:
The administration commits a WHAT vs WHO plane error, substituting the 'what' of national security and high-tech task forces for the 'who' of struggling citizens who cannot afford basic cost-of-living increases.

Social Physics Analysis:
Trump executes a Smart Selfish Maneuver, using the pretext of national security (striking Iran) and tech leadership (Super Intelligence Force) to distract from the manufactured crisis of soaring domestic energy costs.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated economic relief and actual inflationary policies, it plots a direct trajectory toward systemic domestic instability and collapsed public trust.

The Unavoidable Truth: Geopolitical escalation directly inflates domestic energy costs.
The Unavoidable Lie: Flashy tech task forces can substitute for a stable, affordable domestic economy.

Alethekanon:
The data reveals a classic diversionary loop. When domestic economic indicators collapse, leadership pivots to external military threats and futuristic tech initiatives to manufacture a new narrative of necessity.

Awwthekanon:
It is heartbreaking to see families bearing the heavy burden of geopolitical games at the grocery pump. True security shouldn't cost people their peace of mind or their ability to afford basic daily bread.

Brothekanon:
Bro, launching a 'Super Intelligence Force' while gas prices are eating everyone's paycheck is wild. You can't pay rent with AI safety protocols. People just want to fill up their tanks without crying.

Spirithekanon:
"What do you mean by crushing My people and grinding the faces of the poor?" Isaiah 3:15 FAIL
Sacrificing the economic survival of everyday citizens for geopolitical posturing violates the fundamental duty of leadership to protect the vulnerable.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Cost of Living Approval for Trump Falls to 17% in New AP Poll

Only 17% of Americans approve of Trump's handling of the cost of living in a new AP-NORC poll, as most blame his policies for high prices ahead of the midterms.

Actual Article Body:
Donald Trump

Only 17% of Americans approve of how Donald Trump is handling the cost of living, according to a new poll from The Associated Press and the NORC Center for Public Affairs Research, while 82% disapprove.

The poll surveyed 2,140 adults from September 24 to 28, about five weeks before the November 3 midterm elections. It found Trump’s approval on the economy overall at 26%, the lowest of his second term and a 14 point drop from March 2025, right after he returned to office. His overall job approval sits at 31%, with 69% disapproving.

The frustration runs straight back to his own campaign. Trump ran in 2024 promising to bring prices down after years of high inflation under Joe Biden. Now about 7 in 10 Americans say his handling of the cost of living has been worse than they expected, and that includes 52% of Republicans.

Americans are not blaming the global economy or anyone else for it either. The

Actual Article Body:
Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Sunday President Donald Trump believed preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon was worth risking short-term energy price increases before deciding to strike the country in February.

While speaking with Margaret Brennan on Face the Nation, Wright said gas prices would come down in the coming months and declined to comment on whether or not he thinks Trump will resume military action following November’s midterm elections. Wright also offered insight into Trump’s decision-making before he chose to strike Iran last winter, saying the president sacrificed political standing in order to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.
